A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Context-free Recognition with Transformers by the same authors. All 20 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, equations, algorithms, tables and Figure 1, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Table 2 report original transformer-classification experiments on six formal-language tasks, with training details in Appendix C.

after.justification: Section 5 and Table 2 retain the original classification experiments and their accuracy results across seeds, supported by Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the item/slashed-item construction, path-system and pebbling procedures, and transformer architecture are retained. The added ReLU explanation specifies how an existing equality check works without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate infix and postfix BFVP, binary Palindrome, Marked Palindrome, Dyck(1) and Dyck(2), including in-distribution and longer-string evaluations. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the fixed-depth versus log(n)-looped transformer comparison for every language and both test regimes. Newly cited studies do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains one million training samples of length at most 40, 2,000 test samples of length at most 80, the 1.2-million-parameter models, layer configurations and training settings. Expanded sampling explanations document the existing setup without revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The investigations of looping and length generalization are retained. Neither the main text nor appendices add or remove ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations, error analyses or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds in Appendix C and report mean accuracy with standard deviation in Table 2. No uncertainty-reporting practice, run count or statistical test changes.

E6.justification: Every mean and standard deviation in Table 2 is identical. For example, BFVP out-of-distribution accuracy remains 0.88 for fixed-depth and 0.91 for looping. The reported benefits on BFVP and mixed findings on other languages are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds the integer-valued condition supporting exact ReLU equality testing. Appendix B.2 explicitly derives the C-RASP inclusion through temporal counting logic and its transformer expressivity bound. These refine proof justification; theorem statements, resource bounds and construction equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain general CFL recognition with logarithmic looping and O(n^6) padding, reduced resource requirements for unambiguous and linear subclasses, and empirical looping benefits on BFVP. The revised framing does not alter these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially expands interpretation through connections to learned subgrammars, item representations, memory reads and parallel state tracking, and discusses implications for dynamically scaling architectures. It retains the expressivity-versus-learnability qualification but removes the explicit statement that the padding bounds are not known to be tight.

D1.justification: Appendix C expands the brief sampling description with probabilistic grammars, sampling length before strings, and a geometric distribution governing the number of negative-string edits. These improve documentation of retained experiments; the model and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and conclusion substantially broaden positioning around empirical parallel parsing and state tracking, particularly Allen-Zhu and Li, Schulz et al., Liu et al. and Li et al. Section 3 explicitly relates its recursion to Allen-Zhu and Li, while additional references support attention idealization, proof justification, sampling and learnability.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendices A–C remain intact. Local revisions expand the introduction and sampling explanation, consolidate the proofs of Lemmata 3.1–3.2, and organize the rewritten conclusion under three topic headings. An Impact Statement and acknowledgment text are added.

P2.justification: The single-column main text and bibliography become two-column layouts, with resized and repositioned algorithms and Tables 1–2. Appendices use wider single-column layouts. Tables 3–4 and Figure 1 retain their content within the substantially reformatted document.

improvement.justification: The expanded sampling description and local proof justifications improve transparency, while the revised discussion explains connections to observed parallel parsing more concretely. The gains are limited because the scientific results remain stable. Removing the explicit padding-tightness caveat weakens qualification, but the documentation and explanatory improvements provide a modest net benefit.
